issue.title: [bug] Pi provider plugins skip custom auth.apiKey.login

comments.body:
`internal/plugin/pi.js` turned every pi api-key auth into one generic key field (`{ type: "api", label: "API key" }`), so a provider's own `auth.apiKey.login` was never run and the credential its resolver needs — the key plus provider-scoped `env` — could not be made. pi also fabricates a login for every key provider that wrote none, so the package's own login had to be told apart from that one.

The branch keeps the api-key auth a package registered itself (pi-ai's `createProvider`) and offers it as one keyless `api` method, labelled with that auth's `name`: `ask` returns the login's questions one at a time (the same run pi's OAuth sign-in uses), `authorize` finishes the login and keeps the returned `key` and `env` as the account's `metadata.env`, which `toPi` gives back to pi as the credential's `env`. A login that makes no key keeps only the env, and `toPi` then hands pi a credential with no key. GUI and CLI already skip key entry for a keyless method, so no second raw key is asked. A provider that wrote no login keeps magpie's key field, and pi's fabricated "Enter API key" login is not used. A login's `secret` question is now asked as a password prompt.

Branch: [fix/1682-pi-provider-plugins-skip-custom](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/1682-pi-provider-plugins-skip-custom), commit ce71b1563006d95ebde6b780e627110baf3adb7f.

Run, in `internal/plugin` against a real host with the pinned pi 1.2.0: `TestPiProviderOwnKeyLogin` (new) signs in to a fixture provider whose login asks a workspace and returns key+env, and to one that returns the env marker alone — both are one keyless method, the question is asked, the account holds what the login returned, and a request through pi resolves before and after a host restart. With only `pi.js` reverted it fails with `fakepi-own-key's methods = [{Type:api Label:API key Placeholder: Keyless:false}]`; with the change it passes. `go build ./...`, `go vet ./internal/plugin/` and the cross-OS vet/builds pass, and the package suite passes except `TestPluginSOCKSProxy`, which fails the same way on `upstream/main`.

Fork branch, ready to review; it makes no claim on the issue.
